topic: the copy path is capped by aggregate DMA throughput, and the cap is reached

write_path_sweep.reading: write throughput sits at 1.11-1.13 TB/s and does not respond to element width, chunk size, buffer depth or alignment. It is a property of the path, not of a setting.

aggregate_ceiling.breakdown: read alone reaches 2.13 TB/s and write alone 1.13 TB/s, but together they only reach 1.65 TB/s, so the two directions contend for the same movement resource

conclusion: a pure copy of the same 128MB cannot be done faster than about 0.078 ms from TileLang on this host, and our full kernel already runs at 0.0745 ms
the vendor reaches an aggregate 2.43 TB/s, about 47% above the copy-path ceiling we measured
since the byte count is fixed (64MB in, 64MB out, bf16 both ways), the residual gap cannot be closed by arithmetic scheduling, buffer tuning or partitioning within this copy path
this is a measured property of the TileLang copy path on this host, not a claim about the hardware; the vendor evidently uses a movement path we cannot reach from TileLang
